title: Pre-Sleep Integration Review
opening: A brief reverse review can make room for more than the day’s most frustrating moment. It is a recall prompt, not a sleep treatment or a requirement.

source.title: Manuscript, page 44
source.excerpt: Briefly recall the day in reverse. Notice unforced attention, aligned action and distinctions you recognized, along with moments of contraction.
source.attribution: Supplied recovered manuscript. Authorship and adoption of every wording are not independently established.
source.boundary: The reverse order is a prompt for recall, not a proven neurological requirement. Do not turn the review into rumination or a performance audit. If it keeps you awake, shorten it, move it earlier, or omit it.

example.heading: Follow one day in reverse
example.note: This is an illustration, not an observed result. The review adds context without requiring a positive verdict.

moments.label: Enjoyable walk
moments.detail: A walk felt enjoyable. There is no need to explain why before moving back.

moments.label: Useful conversation
moments.detail: A conversation was useful. Notice what was said or done, without turning it into a score.

moments.label: Difficult morning
moments.detail: The morning was difficult. Include it without treating it as the whole day.

example.comparison: One frustrating event can be accurate and still be incomplete. A brief reverse review can include that event alongside other moments; none has to cancel another.

labels.prompt: Recall one event accurately, without evaluating your whole day. Keep this brief.
